o1.text: Welcome to the roast of Nonantum Capital Partners!

o2.text: Tonight we honor five people who've generated incredible returns. Mostly in Excel.

j1.text: First up, the founder himself, Jon Biotti. Jon has three degrees from Harvard.

j2.text: Three! At this point, he's not an alumnus. He's a returning customer.

j3.text: Jon spent twenty years at Charlesbank before leaving to start his own firm.

j4.text: The longest notice period in private equity history.

j5.text: Then he named it after a village in Newton, so nobody would ever pronounce it right. It took me three takes.

d1.text: David Ganitsky went to Harvard, and Stanford.

d2.text: He couldn't decide which coast to feel superior on, so he picked both.

d3.text: Before that, David worked at the Parthenon Group, named after a building that's been under renovation for twenty-five hundred years.

p1.text: Peter Apostolides is our CFO, and our Chief Compliance Officer.

p2.text: So the guy who rejects your expense reports also approves his own. Convenient, Peter.

p3.text: Peter's idea of a wild Friday night is reconciling capital accounts to the penny.

p4.text: Then doing it again. For fun.

s1.text: Shawn Jordan has a master's degree in philosophy.

s2.text: In private equity. Finally, someone who can explain why we're all here. Spoiler: it's the carry.

s3.text: Shawn started as office manager, and now he's vice president.

s4.text: Honestly, the best value creation story in the entire portfolio.

k1.text: Kyle Guinivan worked at McKinsey and Citadel, and went to Wharton.

k2.text: His resume is just a list of places that ruined his weekends.

k3.text: At Citadel, Kyle traded in milliseconds. Now he's in private equity, where a fast exit takes seven years.

k4.text: And he still can't order lunch without a two by two matrix.

c1.text: But seriously. Five brilliant people. One great firm. We love you guys.

c2.text: Now get back to work. Those LPs aren't going to I R R themselves.
